title: stream-wrangler-cancellation-interop-timeout-safety
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Consumers of the Go SDK streaming API see surprising behavior when their local context deadlines or cancellations race with server-side stream termination or network flaky conditions. Current examples show leaked goroutines, partially-acknowledged prefetch windows, and ambiguous error values that make retry/rollback logic fragile.

Goal: Implement a small, well-documented StreamWrangler helper and associated ergonomics so that client code can: (1) attach a configurable "soft deadline" that triggers a graceful drain and detach window before cancelling the underlying transport; (2) ensure cancellations propagate to the server with a reproducible sentinel error; (3) preserve KV/prefetch state where possible for resumable streams; (4) avoid goroutine leaks and make Close semantics deterministic.

Scope: The ticket implements the API surface, internal wiring in the SDK runtime shim, tests, and examples. It does not change server contracts or wire protocol beyond sending a cancellation reason metadata header when available.
technical_design:
Design summary: Introduce a StreamWrangler wrapper around the existing stream iterator. Key concepts: softDeadline (linger window), drainHandshake, cancelReason metadata, sentinel client-side error (ErrStreamCancelledByClient), and normalized error mapping.

Components:
- StreamWrangler struct: wraps the existing Stream and coordinates lifecycle. Exposes Next(ctx) and Close(ctx, reason string).
- Soft deadline helper: WrapContextWithSoftDeadline(ctx, d time.Duration) returns a ctx that, on expiry, triggers a cooperative drain (drainHandshake) and then cancels after linger window. This gives in-flight message handlers time to finish and lets the SDK send a graceful CANCEL metadata to the server.
- Cancel reason propagation: When Close is called or soft deadline expires, StreamWrangler injects an outgoing metadata header X-Client-Cancel-Reason (or uses gRPC/HTTP canonical fields) with a short token (e.g., "client_timeout_soft") to aid server-side debugging and metrics.
- Sentinel error: Define var ErrStreamCancelledByClient = errors.New("stream cancelled by client") and map to codes.Canceled when translating to gRPC/HTTP errors. This makes upstream retry logic straightforward: treat ErrStreamCancelledByClient as a non-transient cancellation unless the caller explicitly retries.
- Leak safety: StreamWrangler installs a bounded goroutine watchdog to ensure any background prefetch or readPump goroutine exits within softDeadline + jitter window. If it doesn't, we log a severe metric and forcibly cancel the transport to avoid resource exhaustion.

API (proposal):
- type StreamWrangler struct { /* opaque */ }
- func NewStreamWrangler(ctx context.Context, s Stream, opts ...StreamWranglerOption) *StreamWrangler
- func (w *StreamWrangler) Next(ctx context.Context) (Message, error) // honors ctx deadlines, returns ErrStreamClosed when stream is finished
- func (w *StreamWrangler) CloseWithReason(ctx context.Context, reason string) error // cooperative close with reason
- func WrapContextWithSoftDeadline(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) context.Context // attaches metadata, triggers graceful drain

Compatibility: Existing code using the raw Stream remains supported. StreamWrangler is opt-in. The helper should be small and well-documented so customers can adopt incrementally.
acceptance_criteria: StreamWrangler is implemented and exported in the go SDK package
WrapContextWithSoftDeadline attaches metadata and triggers drain handshake when the soft deadline fires
CloseWithReason sends a cancel-reason header when transport supports it (unit test mocks ensure header set)
ErrStreamCancelledByClient sentinel is documented and returned on client-initiated cancellations
Unit tests cover graceful drain, forced cancellation after linger window, and watchdog triggering
Integration test demonstrates no goroutine leaks with repeated Start/Close cycles (race-tested)
Example snippet added to README and streaming ergonomics doc page
tasks: spec: finalize API names and options (1d)
implement StreamWrangler core lifecycle and metadata wiring (3d)
unit tests: error mapping, soft deadline, watchdog, CloseWithReason (2d)
integration test: repeated open/close stress test and race sanitizer run (1d)
docs: add examples and migration guide (0.5d)
code review and iterate based on feedback (1d)
release notes and changelog entry for go-sdk-1.9.0 (0.5d)
test_plan:
Unit tests will use a fake transport that simulates slow reads, server-initiated close, and metadata acceptance. Cases to cover:
- Next respects provided ctx deadlines and returns appropriate sentinel errors.
- Soft deadline triggers the drainHandshake path and allows in-flight handler to complete within linger window.
- Forced cancellation after linger window tears down the transport and returns ErrStreamCancelledByClient mapped to codes.Canceled.
- Watchdog triggers if background reader goroutine doesn't exit and results in forced cancel; counter metric is incremented.

Integration tests:
- Run stress test with 1k short-lived streams in a loop for 3 minutes under race detector to surface goroutine leaks.
- Measure that average extra latency introduced by softDeadline flow is within SLAs for normal workloads.

E2E can be validated against staging runtime by enabling client-cancel-reason metadata and checking server logs for the X-Client-Cancel-Reason tag.
rollout_plan:
Feature gated behind go-sdk config flag StreamWranglerEnabled (default false).
- Canary (internal): enable for 10% of internal CI jobs and run stress integration.
- Beta (selected customers): enable for 1-2 early SDK adopters with opt-in flag and collect logs/metrics for cancel-reason headers and watchdog events.
- General availability: flip default to true after 2 weeks of stable canary and customer beta.

Telemetry to collect: number of soft-deadline triggers, average linger window utilization, number of watchdog-forced-cancels, and the distribution of cancel reasons seen server-side.
notes:
Trade-offs considered: full automatic resume semantics were considered but deferred since they require server-side checkpoints and stronger protocol guarantees. We aim for better cancellation ergonomics first and can iterate to add resumability later.

Security: cancel reason tokens are short ASCII strings; avoid leaking PII. Docs and example emphasize using opaque tags (e.g., "signup-flow-timeout") rather than user identifiers.

Open questions:
- canonical header name across HTTP vs gRPC (we currently send both: X-Client-Cancel-Reason and grpc-metadata-x-client-cancel-reason when using gRPC transport)
- should soft-deadline be expressed as absolute timestamp in ctx metadata for better server correlation? (defer)
